In [[commutative algebra]], the '''constructible topology''' on the [[spectrum of a ring|spectrum]] <math>\operatorname{Spec}(A)</math> of a [[commutative ring]] <math>A</math> is a [[topology]] where each [[closed set]] is the [[image (mathematics)|image]] of <math>\operatorname{Spec} (B)</math> in <math>\operatorname{Spec}(A)</math> for some [[Algebra (ring theory)|algebra]] ''B'' over ''A''. An important feature of this construction is that the map <math>\operatorname{Spec}(B) \to \operatorname{Spec}(A)</math> is a [[closed map]] with respect to the constructible topology.

With respect to this topology, <math>\operatorname{Spec}(A)</math> is a [[compact set#Definition|compact]],<ref>Some authors prefer the term ''quasicompact'' here.</ref> [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]], and [[totally disconnected space|totally disconnected]] [[topological space]] (i.e., a [[Stone space]]). In general, the constructible topology is a [[finer topology]] than the [[Zariski topology]], and the two topologies coincide if and only if <math>A / \operatorname{nil}(A)</math> is a [[von Neumann regular ring]], where <math>\operatorname{nil}(A)</math> is the [[nilradical of a ring|nilradical]] of ''A''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lemma 5.23.8 (0905)—The Stacks project |url=https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0905 |access-date=2022-09-20 |website=stacks.math.columbia.edu}}</ref>

Despite the terminology being similar, the constructible topology is not the same as the set of all [[Constructible set (topology)|constructible sets]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://math.stackexchange.com/q/1964351 |title=Reconciling two different definitions of constructible sets|website=math.stackexchange.com|access-date=2016-10-13}}</ref>
